Thanks for the demo, Dylan — concise and helpful. Two quick things from our side: 

1) Performance baseline: can you share TPS and p95/p99 numbers for the candidate models on sequences ~1.2k tokens? We saw some numbers in the deck but would like the raw traces.
2) Prompt set: we'd like to test with our 120-case clinical QA prompts (some will be sensitive). What's the best way to run those securely against recommended models?

Priya and I are aligned that latency matters for our clinical workflow; we want to confirm Redwood can hit sub-250ms p95 on dedicated capacity for the smaller models.

Appreciate a short packet (links + short next steps) — can we aim for tomorrow EOD?

—Alex

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Sharing an initial packet below and a proposed next-step plan. Attachment stubs include the TPS summary and a sanitized prompt pack that you can run in a secure env.

What I'm sending now:
- Redwood-verified performance profiles (link below) covering candidate models we discussed (open-llama-13B, redwood-medium-7B-q4, and opt-6.7b-lite). Profiles include average TPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies at sequence lengths 512 / 1024 / 1280 on RTX A10G and on our Dedicated pool mock.
- medspint_bench_tps_summary.csv (attachment): per-model TPS traces and p95/p99 percentiles for your 1.2k-ish prompt mixes (sanitized).
- medsprint_prompt_set_v1.txt (attachment): the 120-case prompt set with placeholders for PHI; we recommend running in Private or Dedicated with KMS.

Quick read / recommendation: 
- If sub-250ms p95 is a hard SLO for your 1.2k sequences, redwood-medium-7B-q4 (on Dedicated, 1 GPU w/ batching policy aggressive=low-latency) is the best balance. In our Dedicated runs we see p95 ~210–240ms and p99 ~320–360ms depending on KV cache hit rates. TPS (sustained) ~9–12 reqs/sec for your mix.
- open-llama-13B has better quality on nuanced clinical prompts (per our evals) but p95 is typically 350–420ms unless you move to multi-GPU or higher perf nodes.
- opt-6.7b-lite is lower-cost with acceptable precision for triage tasks; p95 ~180–260ms but lower quality on free-response QA.

Security note: To run your real prompts securely we recommend either Redwood Private (VPC + KMS) or Dedicated with a short-lived, scoped ingestion token. I can loop in the Security team if you want SOC2 evidence.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You review the attached prompt pack and medspint_bench_tps_summary.csv — run the prompt set in your staging (we can provide a short-lived Private sandbox).
2) Redwood and Medsprint pick 2 models for a 2-week pilot (suggest: redwood-medium-7B-q4 + open-llama-13B).
3) We'll share a canary plan with traffic split and rollback on model-quality regression.

Ben, adding you for runbook/traces and to own the pilot config. Alex/Priya — want to schedule a 30-min pilot-setup call tomorrow morning?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Alex/Priya — adding the operational traces and short runbook excerpt inline below. I've attached the per-run latency traces (CSV) and a short playbook for guarding against quality regressions during the pilot.

Runbook highlights:
- Canary config: 5% traffic for week 1, 25% week 2, with automated rollback if evaluation metric (EM on clinical QA set) drops >2.5 points vs baseline.
- Batching policy: low-latency (max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=8) for 1-GPU redwood-medium-7B-q4.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated patient-context prompts; this reduces p95 by ~18% in our tests.
- Perf probes: synthetic heartbeat requests (short queries) every 30s to detect tail spikes; alert if p99 > 500ms for 3 consecutive probes.

I've uploaded the detailed traces: [redwood_verified_profiles.md] and a Drive link with raw traces. If you'd like, Grace can run a short smoke test with one of your sanitized cases in the Private sandbox before we flip the canary.

Ben Carter
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
